text: White grabbed the free pawn on e5. Seven moves later, checkmate arrived on f3. The Blackburne-Shilling Gambit looks like a beginner blunder when Black plays 3...Nd4. White thought: "A free pawn on e5 with an attack on f7!" Then came 4.Nxe5? Qg5! and White's king never saw move 8. Greedy play in the opening gets punished fast. The refutation is simple: 4.Nxd4! exd4 5.O-O, leaving White with superior development and complete center control. Review the full refutation and trap defense inside the Academy.
